description:
Tage Thompson has led the Buffalo Sabres in goals in each of the past five seasons, establishing himself as the centerpiece of their resurgence and a driving force behind ending the franchise’s 14-year playoff drought. A towering forward with a lethal release and elite hands, Thompson combines size and skill to consistently overpower defenders and finish at a high level.  He brings a true “wow-factor” every time he touches the puck, capable of producing highlight-reel moments out of tight spaces. In a game against Pittsburgh, Thompson showcased that precision—receiving a pass near the goal line, he quickly stickhandled, pivoted toward the net, and snapped a perfectly placed shot bar down, threading it through a razor-thin gap between the goalie’s mask and the post.

One of the most productive offensive players in the NHL over the past several seasons, Nikita Kucherov continues to cement his place among the league’s elite. The Tampa Bay Lightning right winger’s resume is loaded—multiple Art Ross Trophy wins, a Hart Trophy, two Ted Lindsay Award honors, and two Stanley Cup championships. A proven finisher with four 40-goal seasons in just six years, Kaprizov has a knack for turning chaos into goals.

description:
Leading the league in shutouts with seven, Ilya Sorokin delivered another elite season between the pipes for the New York Islanders, reinforcing his status as one of the NHL’s premier goaltenders. One of his finest performances came in a 44-save shutout against the New Jersey Devils. After turning aside an initial shot from distance, Sorokin tracks the rebound as it kicks out to Jonas Siegenthaler, then explodes across the crease to make a spectacular, acrobatic stop to keep the puck out.
